identification: Cold-painted spelter (or bronze) terrier harnessed to a two-wheeled iron cart with a real murex shell as the body. Austrian-style novelty, c.1900-1920. No maker's mark seen in photos; paint losses to dog and legs, bent harness, minor shell chips.

entries.note: Database hit (hammer, no premium): cold painted Austrian kingfisher bowl and spelter ostrich cart, early 20th C, 12cm; a lot of two pieces, so one cart is worth less. Over 10 years old. Condition unknown. Local database record only, page not opened.

Only one relevant hit (Leski 2015). Other hits were trench art, resin or Beswick dogs, irrelevant. No Armitage/Gowans comparable.
chrome_hint: eBay AU and eBay.com sold/Terapeak: 'cold painted dog cart shell', 'Vienna bronze dog cart shell', 'Austrian cold painted spelter dog pulling cart', 'novelty murex shell cart dog Victorian'. Also Leski, Leonard Joel, Mossgreen, Theodore Bruce and LiveAuctioneers/Invaluable results for 'cold painted Austrian dog cart' and 'Bergmann dog cart'. Check whether the dog is bronze (heavy, Vienna) or spelter (lighter, dull grey where paint lost).
viewing_check: Pick up the dog: weight, and bare metal where paint is lost (golden bronze = Vienna bronze, dull grey = spelter). Check underside of dog and cart for a stamp or cartouche (e.g. B for Bergmann), and that the shell, axle and wheels are original and not a married assembly.
